namgun--academy.scene: INTRODUCING YEON NAMGUN, four years old, Yeon's second son — nobody ever had to teach him to push. A SMALL CHILD, NOT the grown bearded man on the sheet: keep only the sheet's heavy straight brows, narrow fierce eyes and black hair, on a round-cheeked four-year-old's face — no beard, no moustache, no armour, no weapons; a little boy in a small dark-red Goguryeo child's jeogori and trousers, hair in a tiny topknot tied with red cord. Evening at the Yeon family table in Pyongyang. Low angle from across the low table: he kneels up on his cushion, both small fists clamped round the last rice cake, chin jutting, glaring sideways at his big brother off-frame with a ferocious pout — he will not let go first. A clay oil lamp on the table lights him from below in warm deep red (#9e3b32). Behind him, painted loosely in hearth smoke and lamplight: dark timber posts, a red-and-ochre painted wall, a glowing brazier, soft warm bokeh.

euija-king--king-euija.scene: INTRODUCING KING EUIJA, forty-one, crowned this morning — the court will style him Righteous and Merciful, and he finds that funny. Dawn on the river below Sabi, low mist on the water. Low three-quarter angle: he lounges sideways in a carved throne set on the riverbank bluff, one hand still settling the new black-and-gold Baekje crown on his head, watching his own omen rise: out over the river, four long lacquered paper kites tied nose-to-tail into a red-and-gold 'dragon' float in the mist — plainly paper and bamboo, their strings faintly visible. A slow cynical smirk, one eyebrow up, eyes amused and cold: "No, it isn't." A low sunrise shaft rakes across his face and crimson silk from the side in hard amber (#e08a2e). Behind him, painted loosely in rose-gold mist: the river, boats as soft shapes, and a far bank of kneeling crowds dissolving into haze, banners as bokeh.

gyebek-general--king-euija.scene: INTRODUCING GYEBEK, twenty-one, the boy with the borrowed name, grown — he still cannot say a thing he does not believe. Dawn on the misty river below Sabi, the morning of the king's omen. Low three-quarter angle from beside him on the riverbank: he stands at the king's side (only an out-of-focus crimson royal sleeve at the frame edge), turned half toward the camera, one hand resting on the ring pommel of the sheathed sword at his hip, the other pointing flatly out at the river, where four lacquered paper kites tied nose-to-tail as a 'dragon' float in the mist — plainly paper and bamboo, the strings visible. A heavy deadpan scowl, narrow eyes, utterly literal and unimpressed: "…Your Majesty. That is not a dragon." A low sunrise shaft rakes across his face from the side in hard gold (#d9b13a). Behind him, painted loosely: rose-gold river mist, boats and a far bank of kneeling crowds as soft shapes, banners as bokeh.

seongchung--king-euija.scene: INTRODUCING SUNGCHUNG, the minister who asks the question the king hoped nobody would. Night in the king's private hall at Sabi palace, after the omens have been arranged. Low three-quarter angle across a low lacquered table: he kneels at its edge in his gold court robe, leaning forward with both palms flat on the wood, eyes lifted to the king off-frame (only an out-of-focus crimson royal sleeve and a shallow celadon wine bowl at the frame edge), earnest and anxious, brows knotted, mouth open mid-question — asking what happens when the people work it out. His gold silk is brushed in loose, visible, dragging strokes. A single bronze oil lamp on the table lights him from below in warm gold (#c9a24d), the shadows deep. Behind him, painted loosely in lamp smoke and incense haze: dark red pillars, a folding screen, a lattice window with blue night beyond, small warm lantern bokeh.

pung-prince--king-euija.scene: INTRODUCING PRINCE PUNG, seventeen, the quiet prince with the good handwriting — he is about to learn what a hostage is for. A feast night in the great hall at Sabi; the king has just shouted his name across the room. Low three-quarter angle: he rises from his place at a low banquet table, half-standing, one ink-stained hand still on the table edge, back straight, chin lowered in obedience, eyes glistening and too steady — he already knows: "…For how long?" A smooth beardless young face, composure held over fear. Hanging lanterns rake across him from the side in pale gold (#e6c76a). Behind him, painted loosely in feast smoke and warm haze: red pillars, dishes and wine jars as soft forms, the blurred dark shapes of seated courtiers in Baekje silk, lantern bokeh.

yunchung--yunchung.scene: INTRODUCING YUNCHUNG, a frontier general from a family too small to count — that is the point. A winter night in the king's private chamber at Sabi palace; he has ridden in from the Silla frontier, and nobody from the eight houses has been told. Low three-quarter angle: still in his dented helm and road-dirty lamellar, snow melting on the shoulder plates, he sits bolt upright on a too-fine silk cushion, fists planted on his knees, the red-lacquered scabbard of his ring-pommel sword at his hip, answering the king off-frame with a flat, blunt stare and the barest shrug: "…On paper." A brazier at his side lights him from below in hard ochre-gold (#c9932a). Behind him, painted loosely in brazier smoke: lacquered screens, a dark red pillar, and through a lattice window snow falling blue-white in the night as soft cold bokeh.

chunbok--yunchung.scene: INTRODUCING SATEK CHUNBOK, a young lord of the Satek house with good manners and a quick eye for an opening. Spring, the Assembly hall at Sabi, the eight great houses in session. Low three-quarter angle: he makes a courteous half-bow toward the throne off-frame, hands folded inside his wide crimson sleeves, the tall pointed openwork gilt-bronze crown of a Baekje great-clan lord set high over his topknot — but his eyes slide sideways, alert, measuring the room, a polished smile at the corner of his mouth: "As Your Majesty well knows…" A spring sun shaft through the tall open doors rakes across his face and the gilt crown from the side in warm gold (#d4a94e). Behind him, painted loosely in sunlit haze and incense: red pillars, other lords in gilt crowns as blurred shapes, and beyond the doors blossoming trees and a great grey rock as soft bokeh.

kingsung--the-severing.scene: INTRODUCING KING SEONG OF BAEKJE, about fifty, who has lost a river and means to get it back. Draw him as a dignified, weathered Baekje king: a lean face, deep-set grieving eyes under heavy brows, a neat black moustache and short beard streaked with grey, black hair in a topknot under the Baekje king's crown — a tall rounded black silk cap with a black brow band and twin tall openwork gold flame-and-leaf ornaments rising on either side; a crimson robe with a steel lamellar cuirass over it for the march. His head sits low enough in the frame that the whole crown and its gold ornaments stay well inside the picture, with clear sky above them. Dusk on the road toward the Silla border. Low three-quarter angle: he turns in the saddle at the head of his column, one gloved fist tight on the reins, looking back over his shoulder at the river valley he lost, glinting far below; jaw clenched, grief hardening into resolve: "It went into the marrow." The low red-gold sunset (#e5b83a) rakes across his face from the side. Behind him: a vast sunset sky of torn storm cloud painted in loose strokes, the river shining in the valley, banners and spears of his army dissolving into dust.

dodo--the-severing.scene: INTRODUCING DODO, a slave in the Silla camp — remember the name; the annals almost didn't. Night on the ridge road near Gwansan fortress; the captured Baekje king sits on a camp stool just off-frame. Low three-quarter angle, close to the ground: he kneels on one knee in the dirt, having bowed twice the way you bow to a king, and now raises his head — his eyes lifted straight at the king, quiet, steady, terrible; one hand rests on the ring pommel of the plain sheathed sword at his hip: "Let me take the head." A humble face with no fear left in it. Cold blue-grey moonlight (#7f96b5) rakes across his face from the side; behind him, torches carried by Silla soldiers (only dark blurred shapes in Silla hanbok and lamellar) burn as warm orange bokeh in drifting smoke, the dark ridge and the fortress wall a soft silhouette under torn night cloud.

gumil--gumil.scene: INTRODUCING GUMIL, a yellow-sleeve border officer — he does the work, and the purple sleeve signs it. Morning inside the great granary of Daeya fortress. Low three-quarter angle: he sits on a stack of straw rice sacks with a bundle of notched wooden tally sticks across his knee, the ochre-yellow cuff of his rank sleeve showing at his wrist, counting on his thick fingers, and glances up sideways toward the stair to the commander's hall with a sour, sardonic, put-upon grimace: "My pay, Commander." Shafts of cold slate-blue morning light (#6b7f9e) through the slatted timber wall rake across his face and the sacks, dust motes swimming in the beams. Behind him, painted loosely in dusty haze: heaped rice sacks receding into shadow, heavy timber posts, an open grain-door showing a bright sliver of the stone fortress yard.

gumilwife--gumil.scene: INTRODUCING MAEHWA, thirty-one, Gumil's wife — plum blossom, the flower that does not wait for spring. Evening in their poor one-room house inside Daeya fortress. Low three-quarter angle: she lounges on the edge of the low sleeping platform, one knee drawn up, pushing her wood-sprig hairpin back into her coiled hair, and slides a frank, amused, unhurried look sideways at her husband off-frame, a slow half-smile: "They all smell the same." Her green robe loose at the collar as on the sheet; tired, beautiful, unbothered. Cool sage-green dusk light (#8AAFA0) through the paper window rakes across her face and silk from the side, against the small warm glow of a clay lamp. Behind her, painted loosely in hearth smoke: rough mud-and-timber walls, a cracked jar holding a bare plum branch with a few early blossoms, soft lamplit bokeh.

kangrim--siege-of-daeya.scene: INTRODUCING KANGRIM, the underworld's fetch — he asks one question at the door, and he waits for the answer. Night, the inner room of the burning fortress of Daeya; he was not in the room a moment ago, and now he is, at the polite distance of a messenger. Low three-quarter angle: tall and thin in his crow-black robe, the wide black gat brim hiding his eyes entirely — only the mouth and jaw visible; the whole tall gat sits well inside the frame with space above it — he holds a red-covered register open in one hand and reads her name from it aloud for the third time, calm and courteous, almost gentle, about to ask his one question. The pages show no legible writing. Firelight from the burning yard, through the paper lattice, rakes across his jaw and robe from the side in orange, while cold grey smoke (#4a4a58) seeps in around him; the edges of his robe dissolve into ink-brush strokes. Behind him: a smoke-filled timber room, drifting embers, fire glow through the lattice as bokeh.

bojang--yeons-massacre.scene: INTRODUCING KING BOJANG, the old king's nephew — he has been given a crown and very little to do with it. Night in the banquet hall at Pyongyang, minutes after the massacre. Low three-quarter angle: he sits rigidly on the edge of the throne where he has just been put, hands gripping his knees, the Goguryeo gold crown with its upright flame sprays and gold spangles set slightly crooked on his head and fully inside the frame with space above it, shoulders hunched, his eyes WIDE WITH FEAR darting up and sideways toward someone huge just off-frame (only a blurred dark shoulder and red cape at the frame edge); eyebrows raised and pinched together, a bead of sweat at his temple, his mouth caught in a trembling, forced, terrified half-smile as he stammers "M-my name?" — a frightened man pretending to be calm, not a pleased one. Torchlight from below rakes across his face in dull wine-red (#8f4a44). Behind him, painted loosely in heavy smoke: overturned low banquet tables, scattered bronze bowls and lacquer cups (no glassware), spilled wine dark across the floor, plain unmarked red silk hangings (no writing, no characters, no symbols), guttering torches as bokeh — no bodies, no gore.

gesomun-supreme--yeons-massacre.scene: INTRODUCING YEON GESOMUN, thirty-seven, Supreme Commander, in a chair he built himself above every other chair in the room. Night, the banquet hall at Pyongyang, the blood not yet dry. CLOSE low angle from just below the edge of the raised dais, framed from the chest up so his bearded face is LARGE in the frame: he lounges back in a tall new chair set higher than the throne, one heavy forearm draped over the carved armrest, a shallow bronze wine bowl dangling from his fingers as he points idly DOWN at someone below the lens; chin up, a slow, amused, dangerous half-smile: "You there…" Four crow-ring sword hilts fan up over his shoulders from his back. A brazier just beside the dais blasts hard red light (#d0362f) up across his cheekbones, beard and armour plates, the far side of his face falling into deep shadow, every fold and plate laid in with loose visible brushstrokes. Behind him, painted loosely in drifting smoke: plain unmarked red war banners, dark timber pillars, overturned tables, torch bokeh — no signboards, no plaques, no writing or characters anywhere, no gore.

shinsung--yeons-massacre.scene: INTRODUCING SHINSUNG, a young monk of Pyongyang — very quiet, and very well connected. A temple hall in Pyongyang, the morning after the massacre; the new master of the city has just told the monks to pray quieter. Low three-quarter angle: shaven head, no hat, in his red monk's robe, he lowers his head in the smallest bow, palms pressed together with prayer beads looped over his gloved fingers, eyes downcast — then lifts them, calm, unreadable, with the faintest patient smile: "Amitabha." Butter lamps on the altar beside him light his face from below in warm dusty rose-brown (#8f7b70). Behind him, painted loosely in incense smoke: the gilt shoulder of a great Buddha dissolving in haze, red pillars, rows of small lamp flames as soft bokeh, faint grey morning beyond the temple doors — no plaques, no scrolls, no writing anywhere.

taizong--emperor.scene: INTRODUCING THE SECOND EMPEROR OF TANG, forty-five — he owns half the world, and he is curious about the other half. The night audience in the Tang palace at Chang'an; a report from the far east has just been read aloud. Low angle from below the dais: he leans forward on the throne, one elbow on the armrest, a rolled report loose in his fingers (no visible writing), the yellow robe spilling wide and heavy into the dark; eyes narrowed, a predator's slow, interested smile under the beard as he tastes a foreign name: "Gai… Suwen." A bronze lamp-tree beside the dais rakes across his face and the yellow silk from the side in hard amber (#c97a2e), half his face falling into deep shadow; his tall black futou cap sits fully inside the frame. Behind him: a screen painted with misty mountains (no writing, no calligraphy) and vermilion columns melting into incense haze and blue-black night, lamp flames as round gold bokeh, red lantern glow through a lattice.

chusuiliang--emperor.scene: INTRODUCING CHU SUILIANG, the court diarist — he writes down everything the emperor says, which makes him the bravest man in the room. Draw him as a lean Tang scholar-official of forty-seven: a long, calm, narrow face, a neat thin moustache and small chin beard, hooded patient eyes; a black Tang futou cap, a deep crimson round-collared Tang official's robe with a black belt — Tang dress, not hanbok. The night audience in the Tang palace at Chang'an. Low three-quarter angle: he kneels at a low writing desk at the foot of the dais, brush lifted above an unrolled scroll whose paper is still completely blank — not a single character on it — glancing up toward the emperor off-frame (only a blur of imperial yellow silk at the frame edge) with a perfectly deadpan face, about to correct the date on the report. A small oil lamp on his desk lights him from below in muted bronze (#8c7a5b). Behind him: vermilion columns, incense haze, blue-black night, lamp-tree flames as gold bokeh.

weizheng--four-dragons.scene: INTRODUCING THE IMPERIAL MINISTER, sixty-three — his job is to say no, and he is very good at his job. Tonight he is dying. Night in his sickroom in Chang'an. Low three-quarter angle from the bedside: he lies propped on pillows under a dark quilt, gaunt, his long grey-streaked beard over the covers, one thin hand reaching out to grip the emperor's sleeve (only an out-of-focus fold of imperial yellow silk at the frame edge); his eyes clear, stubborn and dry, a crooked, affectionate half-smile — telling the emperor that when he is gone, no one will be left to tell him no. An oil lamp at the bedside lights him from below in warm worn bronze (#9a7b4f). Behind him, painted in loose smoky strokes: gauze bed curtains, steam curling off a medicine brazier, dark lacquer screens and blue night through a lattice, soft lamp bokeh.

lishiji--four-dragons.scene: INTRODUCING THE BLUE DRAGON, the emperor's most patient general — which is its own kind of danger. Dawn over the vast imperial muster field as the army gathers for the invasion. Low three-quarter angle: he sits utterly still in the saddle of a dark horse beneath a huge blue dragon banner (a painted dragon, no lettering), gloved hands resting on the reins, in dark Tang armour with a heavy fur-trimmed mantle, his face half in shadow as on the sheet — a lean, weathered face near fifty, a long thin moustache, eyes hooded, patient and unreadable — watching the muster churn below him as if he has all the time in the world. Cold blue dawn light (#4b78c9) rakes across his face and armour from the side. Behind him: three more huge dragon banners — white, red and black — each showing ONE long sinuous Chinese dragon painted along the cloth (never a round emblem, crest or roundel, no lettering), snapping in the wind, and a sea of spears and dust dissolving into blue-grey haze under a wide pale dawn sky.

xuerengui--four-dragons.scene: INTRODUCING XUE RENGUI, twenty-nine, a poor farmer with good soil for graves — his wife thinks he could do better. Late afternoon in a poor millet field at Longmen. NOT the white armour on the sheet: today he is a farmer in plain, cheap yellow hemp, sleeves rolled to the elbow, hair in a plain topknot tied with a hemp strip, with the sheet's face and goatee. Low three-quarter angle: huge and broad, he leans on a wooden hoe beside a half-raised rammed-earth grave mound, sweat on his brow, turning his head toward the village where the war edict was posted, torn — a humble, troubled face: "The mounds… they're not done." The low golden sun rakes across him from the side, his pale colour (#e8e3d5) in the dusty light. Behind him: golden millet stalks, a mud hut, dusty hills and a wide bright afternoon sky painted in loose warm strokes.

xueliu--four-dragons.scene: INTRODUCING LADY LIU, twenty-seven, a farmer's wife — the farmer has no idea what she has planned for him. Late afternoon at the door of their poor rammed-earth hut at Longmen. Low three-quarter angle: she leans one shoulder against the rough door frame, arms folded, a plain wooden pin in her bun, and looks out at her husband (only a blurred broad shoulder in yellow hemp at the frame edge) with sharp, amused, absolutely decided eyes and the corner of a smile: "You're not a hoe. You're a ji." Plain brown hemp Tang peasant dress as on the sheet. The low golden sun rakes across her face from the side, warm tan dust (#c4a484) hanging in the light. Behind her: the dim hut interior on one side, and outside a golden millet field and a bright, dusty afternoon sky painted in loose strokes.

yangmanchun--yodong.scene: INTRODUCING THE GUARDIAN OF ANSI, the man who holds Ansi — the other side never learns his name, and he never offers it. A bright summer afternoon on the stone wall of Ansi fortress; the Tang emperor has ridden up below to look at him. Low three-quarter angle from the wall-walk: he leans both forearms on a stone crenellation, helmet on, looking DOWN past the camera at the emperor far below with a wry, unimpressed half-smile, one eyebrow cocked — the emperor wants his name, and he will not give it. At his hip only the worn, plain small iron RING pommel of his sheathed sword and a hand's width of grip poke out from under the fold of his red cape — the rest of the hilt and the scabbard are hidden under the cape; no disc, no round guard anywhere. The hard afternoon sun rakes across his face and armour from the side, his red-orange (#e05a3c) in the war cape and the sunlit dust. Behind him: a vast bright sky of towering clouds, plain unmarked red Goguryeo banners (no writing) snapping on the wall, and far below the haze of the Tang host and its earthen siege mound.

dongchun--boiling-river.scene: INTRODUCING KING DONGCHEON OF GOGURYEO, thirty-five — a king who starts a war over a letter. Draw him as a proud, hawk-faced Goguryeo king: a short black beard and moustache, fierce bright eyes, black hair in a topknot under the Goguryeo gold crown — a gold band crowded with upright flame and branch sprays hung with small round gold spangles — over red-edged steel lamellar and a red cape; his head sits low enough in the frame that the whole crown stays well inside the picture. Dawn by the Boiling River, at the head of five thousand horse. Low three-quarter angle: he twists in the saddle toward his riders, raising one open palm and starting to close it into a fist — the enemy's famous general's life in the palm of his hand — with a cocky, reckless grin. The low red sunrise (#8b4040) rakes across his face and the gold crown from the side. Behind him: steam rising off the river in the cold dawn, plain unmarked red cavalry banners (no writing) and lances dissolving in the haze, a wide pale sky streaked with cloud.

yuhwa--haemosu.scene: INTRODUCING LADY YUHWA, the Amnok's youngest river-daughter — heaven is about to ruin her afternoon, or make it. A bright afternoon in the shallows of the Amnok. Low angle from the water's surface: she kneels in the green river with the water at her chest, half turned away from the camera, the wet ice-blue silk still clinging round her and slipping off one bare shoulder, her long black hair twisted in one fist like a dark rope as she wrings the river out of it — and she looks UP over her shoulder at the sky, as if someone up there had said her name: a slow, curious, unafraid half-smile, lips parted, in no hurry. Only bare shoulders above the water. The hard afternoon sun from high at the side rakes across her face and shoulder, and the river's glitter throws ice-blue light (#8fc4e0) up under her chin. Behind her: a vast bright sky of sunlit clouds, reeds and stony banks, green hills, sun-glitter as bokeh.

hwahye--haemosu.scene: INTRODUCING HWAHYE, the eldest river-daughter — first into the water, every time. The same bright afternoon in the Amnok shallows; a shadow has just crossed the sun. Low angle at the water's surface: she stands in the green river up to her collarbones, only her bare shoulders above the water, wet black hair plastered down under her pearl hairpin, and snaps her head round toward her sisters off-frame with a curt, stern, protective frown, one hand slicing the water — "Hey. In. Now." — already turning to dive. Her pale silk lies neatly folded on a sunlit rock behind her. The hard afternoon sun rakes across her face from the side; the cloud shadow sweeping the water behind her goes violet (#8a62c4). Behind her: a bright sky of sunlit towering clouds, reeds, stony banks, sun-glitter on the river as bokeh.

wihye--haemosu.scene: INTRODUCING WIHYE, the middle river-daughter — she laughs first and dives second. The same bright afternoon in the Amnok shallows. Low angle at the water's surface: up to her collarbones in the green river, only her bare shoulders above the water, long wet black hair flinging droplets as she twists round, laughing helplessly at her little sister off-frame, eyes squeezed half-shut with mischief, mouth open mid-tease — "Pfft—" — a splash ring just ahead of her where her elder sister has already dived. The hard afternoon sun from the side rakes across her face and the flying droplets, and the river throws green light (#4fad72) up under her chin. Behind her: a bright sky of sunlit clouds, reeds and stony banks, her silk tossed carelessly on a rock, sun-glitter as bokeh.
